buildsOn: refactor/one-page-portfolio (PR #256, draft - blog modals + 301 redirects, build broken on CI)
summary: Convert the Namias portfolio into a true one-page resume. All content lives on / and is presented in a compact 2-column resume layout (header on top, ~38% left column for contact/skills/education, ~62% right column for summary/experience/projects). Deep content (resume PDF, blog list, blog post, project detail, role detail, contact form, booking) opens as modals. /blog was already removed in the precursor branch; /contact was never a route (always a modal). No new routes are added. The precursor branch's modal work is folded in; this branch adds the Suspense boundary fix that unblocks the failing CI checks (CodeQL, Vercel, Workers Builds) and the visual redesign.
narrative: The portfolio is a Next.js 16 App Router site. The current public surface is /, /studio, and /api/*. PR #256 (precursor) removed /blog and added blog modals, but it broke the static prerender of /_not-found because useSearchParams() in ModalAutoOpen is not wrapped in a Suspense boundary. This causes CodeQL Analysis, Vercel, and Workers Builds to all fail with the same error. This branch fixes that build error and, in parallel, redesigns the / page to feel like a clean, scannable resume. The current 2-column grid with sticky sidebars is replaced by a tighter compact 2-column layout that reads top-to-bottom. The goal: simplicity and directness. A visitor lands on / and sees the equivalent of a one-page CV with everything reachable in two clicks (or zero, for inline details).
principles: Only one public content page: /. /studio is the CMS (admin). /api/* is the backend. Nothing else.
Resume-like, not marketing-page-like — header on top, two compact columns below, no sticky sidebars, no heavy card wrappers between sections.
Modals, not routes — every deep view (resume PDF, blog, project, role, contact, booking) opens in a modal.
Preserve SEO — /blog/:slug 301s to /?modal=blog-post&slug=:slug so old inbound links keep working.
Fix the build first — the Suspense boundary around ModalAutoOpen unblocks all three failing CI checks. The visual redesign can be reviewed independently once the build is green.
Each slice is a commit — Suspense fix, home page redesign, test updates, docs are all separate commits.
No regression — 269/269 tests stay green, react-doctor stays at 0 diagnostics.

risks.risk: useSearchParams() bails out the static export for any page that contains the Providers tree. The /_not-found page is the one that breaks first because it's auto-generated.
risks.mitigation: Wrap ModalAutoOpen in <Suspense fallback={null}>. This is the standard Next.js fix and is documented in the official error message.

risks.risk: The visual redesign could break the existing visual design language or the 62%/38% grid that the user liked.
risks.mitigation: Use a 38%/62% compact 2-column grid (similar to the existing 62%/38% but inverted roles for the new context). Keep Card wrapper on the hero; use <hr> between sections inside one big wrapper. Avoid changing the colour palette or typography.

risks.risk: The 2-column layout may not fit well on mobile.
risks.mitigation: Stack to single column below 1024px. The 2-column split only applies at lg breakpoint. This is the same pattern as the current 62%/38% grid.

risks.risk: The Suspense fix might unmount ModalAutoOpen between transitions and cause double-open on the same modal.
risks.mitigation: The lastHandled ref already guards against re-opening the same modal twice. Tested in PR #256 with 4 ModalAutoOpen tests.

risks.risk: Closing PR #256 might be seen as wasted work.
risks.mitigation: PR #256's commits are folded into the new branch. The new branch's history will include all of PR #256's commits plus the new work. The PR body will reference PR #256 as a precursor.
